 The Nevada football team plays Northern Illinois at Huskie Stadium on Saturday. Nevada Sports Net’s Chris Murray breaks down the game against the Huskies with his three keys to victory and prediction. This feature is presented in partnership with Bradley, Drendel & Jeanney .
 Nevada (3-5, 2-2 MW) at Northern Illinois (0-9, 0-5) 
 When: Saturday, 12:30 p.m. Pacific time (2:30 p.m. local)
 Where: Huskie Stadium (capacity 28,211) in DeKalb, Ill.
 Surface: AstroTurf
 Weather: High of 44; low of 27
 TV/Radio: None/105.7 FM
 Online: MW+
 Betting line: Nevada by 7.5 points; total of 47.5
 All-time series: Series is tied 1-1
 Last matchup: Nevada won, 35-31, on Oct. 1, 1994 (in DeKalb, Ill.)
 Three keys to the game 
 1. Run for 200-plus yards: Nevada’s run game has gone offline, with the Wolf Pack held to 266 rushing yards over its last four contests. That’s 66.5 yards per game. Three of those four contests have come against defenses that rank in the top eight in the nation in scoring defense, so the sledding has been tough. The sledding will be smoother this week as NIU allows 203.9 run yards per game. Only seven FBS teams have been worse. Nevada is expected to play more with a tight end in this game after going with a spread approach following the season-ending injury to starting TJ DJ Asiasi last month. The Wolf Pack must (and should be able to) establish the ground game, which will take some pressure off a passing attack that ranks last in the nation in efficiency with more interceptions (12) than touchdowns (eight).
 2. Third-down success: There are a lot of areas where NIU struggles, one notable one being third-down defense. The Huskies allow opponents to convert 54.4 percent of their third downs. Nobody in the nation is worse. This should help a Nevada offense that ranks 105th in the country in third-down offense, converting just 35.4 percent of those players into first downs. Nevada converted just 2-of-15 third downs last week against New Mexico (and 5-of-16 the week before against UCLA). As noted in our first key, the Wolf Pack should be able to run the ball and get into third-and-short situations, and NIU has been unable to get off the field on that crucial down for most of the success. This is a stat to watch as Nevada’s offense looks to rebound after tallying just three points over the last two games.
 3. Rein in Rogers: The strength of NIU is its offense, which has averaged 21.8 ppg over the last month (four games) after being stuck at 9.5 ppg in its first four contests against FBS competition. The Huskies have arguably the MW’s best wide receiver in DeAree Rogers, who leads the conference in receptions (70) and receiving yards (719) while scoring five touchdowns. A former Division II player, Rogers is only 5-foot-11 and 200 pounds but is easily the best player on the team and QB Taron Dickens’ top target. Nevada has not played many teams this season that can effectively throw the ball, but Rogers could pose problems for a Nevada secondary that will be without starting CB Bryson Snelling (hand).
 Prediction 
 Nevada 30, Northern Illinois 20: I was going to repeat what I wrote in the UTEP three keys to victory and prediction, which was: “If Nevada loses this game, it should cancel the remainder of the 2026 season.” But I could see the Wolf Pack losing this one. Yes, NIU is the only winless team in the FBS. Yes, NIU has been blown out in most of its games. Yes, NIU lost to an FCS team. But so did Nevada. And while NIU’s defense and special teams function as well as Microsoft Outlook did on Thursday, the Huskies have some pieces on offense. They’ve also played better in the last two games, a seven-point loss at UNLV and 11-point loss at SJSU. I could see NIU making this game interesting. But let’s be blunt: If Nevada loses this game, it should cancel the remainder of the 2026 season. Season record: 6-3 (straight up); 3-6 (against the spread)
